title: 第 38 課｜剛體的接觸：滾動與非完整約束｜Landau–Lifshitz 經典力學
description:
剛體平衡的條件很簡單：作用在它上面的力總和為零，力矩總和也為零。既然總力為零時力矩與原點的選取無關，原點就可以隨便挑。若干個剛體互相接觸時，每一個都要各自滿足這兩個條件，其中要把別的物體在接觸點上施加的力算進去；這些接觸力叫做反作用力，而任兩個物體之間的反作用力大小相等、方向相反。一般來說反作用力的大小與方向要靠解全部物體的平衡方程才知道，但有時方向是給定的：如果兩個物體可以在彼此表面上自由滑動，反作用力就垂直於接觸面。兩個接觸的物體有相對運動時還會出現摩擦，運動分成兩類——滑動與滾動。滑動時反作用力垂直於表面，摩擦力沿著表面；純滾動則完全不同，接觸點沒有相對運動，所以每一瞬間滾動的物體就像被固定在那一點上，反作用力可以指向任何方向，而滾動摩擦表現為一個阻礙滾動的力矩。如果滑動摩擦可以忽略，表面稱為完全光滑；如果只可能純滾動而且滾動摩擦可以忽略，稱為完全粗糙——這兩種情況下摩擦都不會出現在方程裡，問題保持純力學。接觸會減少自由度：自由剛體有六個自由度，放在面上剩五個，純滾動的球只剩三個。但用比自由度更少的座標並不一定辦得到。滾動條件說的是接觸點的速度相等，一般而言這是速度之間的一組線性關係，係數只依賴座標。如果這些關係的左邊不是某個座標函數對時間的全導數，它們就不能積分成座標之間的關係，也就不能真的減少座標的個數——這種約束叫做非完整約束。平面上滾動的球就是標準例子：讓它沿著一條封閉路徑滾一圈回到原地，球的朝向卻已經不同。因此必須保留不獨立的座標，回到最小作用量原理，用不定乘子把約束加進去，得到多帶一個乘子項的運動方程；另一種等價的做法是達朗貝爾原理，直接把反作用力寫進去。

本影片為《Landau–Lifshitz 經典力學》教學系列第 38 課（繁體中文版）。

title: Lesson 38 | Rigid Bodies in Contact: Rolling and Non-Holonomic Constraints | Landau–Lifshitz
description:
The conditions of equilibrium for a rigid body are simply that the total force and the total torque acting on it both vanish. Since the torque is independent of the choice of origin when the total force is zero, any origin will do. When several rigid bodies are in contact, each must satisfy both conditions on its own, counting the forces the others exert at the points of contact. These contact forces are called reactions, and the reactions between any two bodies are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction. In general their magnitudes and directions follow only from solving the equilibrium equations for all the bodies together, but sometimes the direction is given in advance: if two bodies can slide freely over each other, the reaction is normal to the surface of contact. When two bodies in contact move relative to each other, friction appears as well, and the motion divides into two kinds, sliding and rolling. In sliding the reaction is perpendicular to the surfaces and the friction is tangential to them. Pure rolling is quite different: there is no relative motion at the point of contact, so at every instant the rolling body is as if fixed to that point, the reaction may then point in any direction, and rolling friction appears as a torque opposing the roll. If sliding friction is negligible the surfaces are called perfectly smooth; if only pure rolling is possible and rolling friction is negligible they are called perfectly rough. In both of these cases friction never enters the equations and the problem remains purely mechanical. Contact reduces the number of degrees of freedom: a free rigid body has six, one resting on a surface has five, a sphere in pure rolling has three. Choosing coordinates matching that number, however, may be impossible. The rolling condition is that the contact points have equal velocities, which in general is a set of linear relations among the velocities whose coefficients depend only on the coordinates. If the left-hand sides of those relations are not total time derivatives of functions of the coordinates, they cannot be integrated into relations among coordinates alone and so cannot really reduce the number of coordinates. Such constraints are called non-holonomic, and a sphere rolling on a plane is the standard example: roll it once round a closed path back to where it started and it is pointing somewhere else. One must therefore keep coordinates that are not independent, return to the principle of least action, and add the constraints with undetermined multipliers, which gives equations of motion carrying one extra multiplier term. An equivalent route is d'Alembert's principle, which writes the reactions in explicitly.

Lesson 38 of the Landau–Lifshitz Classical Mechanics teaching series (English edition).
